producer.provenance: captured PyTorch with deliberate logging fault

findings.title: Diverged (non-finite values)
findings.message: train/loss became NaN at step 60 (20 non-finite point(s) in this run).
fixes: Lower the learning rate; this is the single most common cause.
Enable gradient clipping if it isn't already on.
Check for a divide-by-zero or log(0) in the loss (e.g. an unstable custom loss term, an empty batch after filtering).
If using mixed precision, check the loss-scaler didn't overflow, or try bf16 instead of fp16.

findings.title: Setback
findings.message: train/loss left a level of 1.014 at step 70, rose to 4.308, and was back by step 100: 30 steps (17% of the run) above a level it had already reached, with 81% of the run's progress given back at the worst point.
fixes: Look at what changed at the first step: the learning rate, a new data shard, an epoch boundary.
Lower the peak learning rate or clip gradients if the rise follows a large update.
If this was a planned restart or curriculum stage, it is expected.

findings.title: Isolated loss spikes
findings.message: train/loss had 1 isolated point well above the level around it; the largest was 5.5 at step 70 against a level of 4.308, 29% of the run's progress.
fixes: Usually one hard or malformed batch. Look at the data at that step if it recurs.

findings.title: Plateau
findings.message: train/loss barely moved from step 20 to 59 (40 points, range 1-1).
fixes: If this is early training, check warmup finished and LR reached its target.
Try a higher LR, an LR-range test, or a different schedule (cosine/one-cycle) if the plateau is unexpected.

findings.title: Diverged (rose from the start)
findings.message: train/loss started around 1 and ended at 3, 3.0x higher, without ever settling below its first level.
fixes: Lower the learning rate; a loss that climbs from the first step is usually an LR an order of magnitude too high.
Add LR warmup and gradient clipping.
Check the loss is the quantity being minimized (sign, reduction, label alignment).

findings.title: Diverged (did not recover)
findings.message: train/loss ended at 4 after reaching 1 around step 20. It has been above that level since step 60 and the log ends with 75% of the run's progress given back.
fixes: Use a checkpoint from around step 20, before the rise.
Lower the learning rate or restart from the last good checkpoint before this window.
Check the LR schedule isn't re-warming up unintentionally (see lr_schedule detector).
Look for a data distribution shift at this step range (new shard, curriculum stage change).

findings.title: Loss spike
findings.message: train/loss jumped to 4 at step 70 from a level of 1, 75% of the run's progress, for 1 logged point.
fixes: Lower the learning rate or add/extend LR warmup.
Clip gradients (or lower the existing max-norm).
Check the batch at this step for a data or tokenization bug (e.g. an unmasked pad token, a corrupted shard).
If the level came straight back and it doesn't recur, it may be one bad batch.
